div.div:
Who owns what
The controller owns builds: it derives a build ID from the pod template, creates one Deployment per build, ramps new workflows onto it through the Temporal API and deletes it once drained. KEDA owns replicas: spec.replicas is absent from both WorkerDeployments, and each build's ScaledObject (rendered from order-fulfillment-scaler / checkout-abandon-scaler) sets 1–3 pods from that build's own backlog. The only replica write the controller keeps is the sunset: drained + 1 h → 0, then delete.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1138px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1135px; margin-left: 12px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#475569, #9ba7b8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Out of this picture
The order worker also runs the start-outbox dispatcher, which retries a workflow start the API could not make inline (docs/api/temporal.md § How the Saga Gets Started). Both workers and the server export telemetry: worker SDK metrics go OTLP to the collector and on to vmagent; the server's ServiceMonitors are scraped by vmagent. The KEDA board (Grafana uid keda) graphs backlog, desired vs current replicas per build.
